messages:
mike: Quick Q — should we surface SLOs/alerting thresholds in Console per-route? I'm worried teams will set tight p99/p95 and blow up oncall with noisy alerts.

tara: +1 on surfacing. But we should provide sensible defaults and a simulation tool (show expected alert rate for a given threshold). Most folks will copy the first thing they see.

kevin: My main fear is noise. If a route has low traffic, 99.9% over a 30d window could mean one spike = page. We need default "don’t page for single small blips" behavior.

sudha: Agreed. Also need per-organization defaults and a RBAC knob so product teams can't escalate paging to infra by mistake. Notifications should be configurable: slack channel, pagerduty, email.

sam: What about adding an estimate hover: enter target + window + breach duration -> estimate alerts/day based on historical distribution. We can compute using existing traces/ingest.

ellie: UI idea: show a slider for target (99 -> 99.99) and a live counter "expected alerts per month". Also offer a toggle "sustained only" (only alert if breach > X minutes).

mike: +1 to sustained. We should also let users set severity levels (info/warn/critical) that map to paging vs channel-only.

oncall-bot: reminder: current oncall policy pages for severity==critical to PagerDuty primary. All other severities post to #eng-oncall.

kevin: We should define a default policy: critical -> page, warn -> slack, info -> telemetry-only. Teams can override but org-admins can lock paging rules.

sam: Backend note: to estimate alert rate we need a small job that replays request latency distribution per-route and counts simulated breaches. Can be cheap if we keep summary histograms.

sudha: API shape suggestion (for product + infra):

```
{
  "slo": {
    "target": 0.995,
    "window": "30d",
    "alert_after": "5m",
    "notify_channels": ["#eng-oncall", "pagerduty:team"]
  }
}
```

ops-bot: FYI we already store HDR histograms in metrics-store for each model+route, so simulation should be feasible without ingesting raw traces.

ellie: Another UX point: surface historical false-positive rate per SLO suggestion (e.g., "expected 3 false positives/month") so teams see noise impact.

mike: How do we avoid over-surfacing complexity? We want quick defaults but an "advanced editor" for power users.

tara: Proposal: default quickflow = pick template (SRE-friendly, Product-friendly, Quiet) -> show simulated alert volume -> accept. Advanced opens full editor with JSON.

kevin: Also need an easy "mute for release" button in Console that creates a temporary suppression window for a route or model. Very common during rollouts.

sam: Yeah, and tie that into rollout UI: when you start a canary, offer to auto-mute alerts for the canary window or route them to a separate channel.

mike: Action items: tara mock quickflow + slider, sudha define API + RBAC, sam prototype estimator using HDR summaries, ellie mock UI copy + simulation visualization. I'll create ticket and assign.

mike: Any objections?

kevin: No objections. Just please make the pager mapping conservative by default.

tara: Will do mockups by EOD Friday.

sudha: I'll draft the API PR next week.

oncall-bot: note: created incident-suppress template in ops-runbook (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/incident-suppress)

mike: :thumbsup: Thanks y'all. We'll iterate after initial mockups.
